body: Quick pass (UMA): quick gate green on the final head (only the changed test is gate-mapped for .cps), plus every camcraft-post suite and 9 rotary/post app suites by hand, clippy clean, no golden moved, the pin fails against the upstream script, body complete. Flagged ready for an independent review at the effort:high tier (posted G-code).

<!-- pr-reviewer: d73477bcd4e1d1b8bef7782ddae9d1703536e038 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

High-tier review (posted G-code). Trial-merged with current `origin/main` (6a10c5ad): clean, no conflicts.

### What looks good
- The new checks sit inside `tilt()` before any word is built, and `onRapid` / `onLinear` / `onCircular` all call `tilt()` and return on `null` before `ensureRotaryUnclamped()` or `block(...)`. So no partial block, and no `M11`, is written before the refusal (`assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps:314-322`, `:687-711`).
- `missingLetter` runs before the C check. A turning C on a machine with no C gets the "states no C rotary" name, and a stated C (millturn.mch) gets the "writes only an A rotary" name. Both are refused once per program through `tiltRefused`.
- B: a turning B on the indexing path is still refused by the earlier `:306` check ("tilted move on a machine without a tilting rotary"). It is not dropped.
- Zero angles: A0 with B0 and C0 on a machine with no rotaries, and on millturn.mch, give no angle word and no warning (probed below). This matches #1092.
- grep for string-built rotary words in `doosan-dnm.cps` and `fanuc.cps` (`"[ABC]" +`, `w("[ABC]"`, `fu(p.[ABC])`): the only one left is the probe macro `ax + fu(pos)` (`:864`), and its `ax` comes from `["X","Y","Z"]`. `fanuc.cps` `tilt()` refuses every non-RTCP tilt (`:141-144`). The decision file's claim holds.
- The pinning test fails without the fix. I reverse-applied the script hunk locally and got `left: [] right: ["indexed move commands A - the machine states no A rotary"]`, then restored it.
- Changelog line, decision file and `Fixes #1155` are present. No process files changed and no goldens moved.

### Local results (merged with main)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all suites, including `script_doosan_dnm` 9, `cycle_hop` 7, `post_engine` 33, `recorded_streams` 10) | all pass |
| `camcraft-app --test doosan_dnm_post` | 10 passed |
| `--test fourth_axis_pose` | 9 passed |
| `--test conformance` (every builtin x every golden, byte-exact, so the Doosan goldens are included) | 6 passed |
| `--test probe_spindle_stop` | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test doosan_dnm_post -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **The third block of the pinning test does not exercise the changed path.** `machine::mirror` sets `rtcp: true` for any rotary whose direction is off the Z column (`crates/post/src/post/machine.rs:282-292`). `doosan-dnm.mch`'s A is about X, so it posts through the RTCP branch, not the indexing branch. A local probe on that machine prints `G43.4 H01` before `M11 / G00 X0 Y0 Z10 A90 / M10`, and the test's line filter hides it. So "a machine that states A posts byte-identically" is true, but the evidence comes from the unchanged RTCP code. The same mirror rule means the indexing path is reachable only on a machine with no off-Z rotary: no rotaries, or a Z-column C as in millturn.mch. An A reaches it only through a rotary stated with a Z or unstated direction. On every shipped machine this path now refuses any turning A or C. That is correct (before, it posted an A the control lacks, or dropped C), but the PR body and the decision file describe this branch as the DNM's clamp/unclamp 4th-axis path. Worth one sentence in the decision file. If you want the byte-identity pinned on this branch itself, add a fixture with a non-tilting stated A.
2. **New refusal for programs that posted before.** millturn.mch (states C about Z) with this post: a turning C used to post with C silently dropped, which was wrong output, and is now refused by name. No shipped machine is bound to this post with a C, and the Changelog line already says "or a turning C, which the indexing path never wrote". Good.
3. The probe on `doosan-dnm.mch` with a later C-turning record (RTCP path, unchanged by this PR) writes the earlier blocks and then refuses. The in-app gate blocks the whole program on any warning, so nothing reaches the machine.

Only a real control can prove: none of the changed lines can reach a DNM's A table, so a real Doosan has nothing new to prove here.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
